children: U.S. Construction Spending Slipped in July
U.S. construction spending ticked down in July, coming in cooler than surveyed analysts had expected, according to the latest report from the Census Bureau.

In its monthly report published Tuesday, the agency said spending on building projects came in at a seasonally adjusted rate of $2.16 trillion in July, down 0.5% from a revised June estimate of $2.17 trillion. Analysts surveyed by The Wall Street Journal had expected spending to stay flat with the prior month.

The annualized pace of private construction was at a seasonally adjusted rate of $1.61 trillion in July, also half a percentage point lower than the prior month. Residential construction was at a seasonally adjusted rate of $859 billion in July, down 1.3% from June.

Annualized spending in the public sector was $543.4 billion in July, which is a 0.2% drop from the revised June estimate of $544.7 billion. Highway construction was $150.3 billion, 0.2% below the revised estimate for June, and $112.3 billion was spent on schools, also down 0.2% from the prior month.
